misconception: You must re-explain your procedures to Claude from scratch, every single time.

mentorLessons.line: If you've pasted the same procedure twice, stop. Fold it into a skill once — Claude picks it up whenever the work calls for it.
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md at its heart. The frontmatter description is the hinge — say what it does *and* when to use it.
Claude reads descriptions to decide when a skill applies. You can also call one by name with a slash — or forbid Claude from ever firing it on its own.
A well-made skill whispers before it speaks: only its name and description sit in context until the work actually needs it.
Anthropic ships ready-made skills — Excel, Word, PowerPoint, PDF. They wake on their own when the task fits; you never summon them by hand.
Personal skills live in your home folder and follow you to every project; project skills live in the repo and serve only that workshop.
A skill is one tool. A plugin is the whole toolbox — skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers — packed and versioned so others can install it.
A marketplace is a catalog, not an installer. Add the catalog, then choose each plugin deliberately — and only from hands you trust.
Instructions for every chat, project knowledge for standing context, a skill for the procedure you reach for again and again.

questions.prompt: Every release, you paste the same 40-line deployment checklist into Claude Code. What do the docs recommend instead?
choices: Keep pasting it — Claude needs procedures re-explained every session
Turn it into a skill: a SKILL.md whose instructions load whenever they're needed
Append it to every prompt with a text-expander macro
Ask Claude to permanently memorize it into the model
questions.reteach: Repeatedly pasting the same instructions is the textbook signal to fold them into a skill instead.
hardChoices: Add it to CLAUDE.md so it loads into context at the start of every session
Package it as a plugin first — single procedures must ship as plugins
Put it in project knowledge so it's always loaded in every conversation

questions.prompt: A section of your CLAUDE.md has quietly grown into a 60-line multi-step procedure. Per the skills docs, what does that signal?
choices: Nothing — CLAUDE.md is the right home for long procedures
Split CLAUDE.md into two memory files
Move it into a skill, since a skill's body loads only when it's used
Delete it and trust Claude to infer the steps
questions.reteach: When CLAUDE.md content becomes a procedure rather than a fact, move it to a skill so it only costs context when used.
hardChoices: Keep it in CLAUDE.md but add keywords so Claude matches on it like a description
Convert it to custom instructions so it applies across every conversation
Move it to a plugin's MCP server config so it loads on demand

questions.prompt: You're authoring a SKILL.md. Which frontmatter field does Claude match your requests against when deciding whether to load the skill?
choices: name
description
version
allowed-tools
questions.reteach: The description — what the skill does and when to use it — is what Claude uses to decide when the skill applies.
hardChoices: The SKILL.md body, which Claude scans before deciding to load
trigger-keywords, a dedicated frontmatter list of match terms
The skill's directory name, matched against the user's words

questions.prompt: Which of these is a valid skill `name` under the Agent Skills format?
choices: Brand Guidelines (Q3)
BRAND_GUIDELINES
brand-guidelines
claude-brand-helper
questions.reteach: Skill names use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only — and can't contain 'claude' or 'anthropic'.
hardChoices: brand_guidelines
Brand-Guidelines
anthropic-brand-kit

questions.prompt: You wrote a /deploy skill with real side effects, and you never want Claude firing it on its own judgment. Which frontmatter line does that?
choices: user-invocable: false
context: fork
paths: none
disable-model-invocation: true
questions.reteach: disable-model-invocation: true means only you can trigger the skill; user-invocable: false restricts the opposite direction.
hardChoices: user-invocable: true
model-invocation: false
auto-trigger: false

questions.prompt: Your new skill never activates when teammates ask related questions. Per the docs, the first fix is:
choices: Rewrite the description to include keywords people would naturally say
Rename the skill directory to something longer
Reinstall Claude Code from scratch
Have everyone paste the skill's contents into chat manually
questions.reteach: If a skill won't trigger, sharpen its description with the words users actually say — that's what Claude matches against.
hardChoices: Move the trigger keywords into the SKILL.md body so Claude scans them
Set disable-model-invocation: true so the skill loads more eagerly
Convert the skill into a plugin — plugins trigger more reliably

questions.prompt: You have thirty skills installed. What actually sits in Claude's context at the start of a session?
choices: The full body of all thirty skills
Each skill's name and description only — full instructions load when a skill is invoked
Nothing at all until you type a slash command
One random skill chosen at startup
questions.reteach: Only lightweight metadata loads up front; a skill's full instructions enter context when it's actually used.
hardChoices: Each SKILL.md in full, but not their bundled reference files
Only the skills you've marked as user-invocable in frontmatter
The five most recently used skills' full instructions

questions.prompt: A skill bundles a large reference.md and a validate.py script. When does the script's source code enter Claude's context?
choices: At session start, along with all skill files
The moment the skill triggers
It doesn't have to — Claude can execute the script and only its output enters context
Never — skills can't include scripts
questions.reteach: Bundled scripts are executed, not read into context — only their output takes up tokens.
hardChoices: When the skill triggers, since all bundled files load together
At install time, when Claude indexes the skill's contents
Only after Claude reads reference.md, which pulls in the script

questions.prompt: In the Claude app, a teammate asks for 'a formatted spreadsheet of Q3 results.' What handles the file creation?
choices: They must first author a custom skill for spreadsheets
A plugin must be installed from a marketplace
Nothing — Claude can't produce spreadsheet files
Anthropic's pre-built xlsx skill, which Claude invokes automatically when relevant
questions.reteach: Anthropic-created document skills activate automatically when the task fits — no setup or re-explaining needed.
hardChoices: The xlsx skill, but only after the teammate invokes it with a slash command
A spreadsheet plugin installed from the Anthropic marketplace
Project knowledge containing spreadsheet formatting instructions

questions.prompt: Which document formats do Anthropic's pre-built document skills cover?
choices: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF
Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma, and Sketch
Markdown, HTML, CSS, and JSON
Keynote, Pages, Numbers, and RTF
questions.reteach: The Anthropic-authored document skills are xlsx, docx, pptx, and pdf — Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF.
hardChoices: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Google Docs
Word, PDF, Markdown, and CSV
Excel, PDF, HTML, and plain text

questions.prompt: In Claude Code, you want one skill available in every project you open, and another only inside a single repo. Where do they go?
choices: Both in the repo's .claude/skills/
Both in ~/.claude/skills/
Personal: ~/.claude/skills/ — project-only: that repo's .claude/skills/
Skills can only be delivered through plugins
questions.reteach: ~/.claude/skills/ follows you across all projects; a repo's .claude/skills/ applies to that project only.
hardChoices: Personal: the repo's .claude/skills/ — project-only: ~/.claude/skills/
Both in ~/.claude/skills/, with a projects: field limiting one to the repo
Personal: CLAUDE.md in home — project-only: the repo's CLAUDE.md

questions.prompt: Your skill needs a long API reference and a set of worked examples. Best structure per the docs?
choices: Inline everything into one giant SKILL.md
Keep SKILL.md lean and reference separate supporting files that load only when needed
Paste the reference into chat at the start of each session
Move the reference into CLAUDE.md instead
questions.reteach: Keep SKILL.md focused and point to supporting files, so heavy detail loads only when it's needed.
hardChoices: Put the reference in the description so Claude sees it before triggering
Split it into several small skills, one per worked example
Store the reference in project knowledge and keep only steps in SKILL.md

questions.prompt: Beyond skills, what can a Claude Code plugin package?
choices: Nothing — plugins are just renamed skills
Only MCP server configurations
Only slash commands
Agents, hooks, and MCP servers alongside skills
questions.reteach: A plugin is a bundle: it can ship skills plus agents, hooks, and MCP servers in one installable unit.
hardChoices: Skills and agents, but hooks must be configured per-user
Anything except MCP servers, which always install separately
Skills plus custom instructions and project knowledge

questions.prompt: Your team wants your five workflow skills in every repo, versioned and easy to update. Docs-recommended route?
choices: Email a zip of your .claude folder around
Package them as a plugin and distribute it through a marketplace
Have each teammate re-teach Claude the workflows in every session
Paste all five skills into each repo's CLAUDE.md
questions.reteach: Plugins are the sharing unit — installed plugin skills arrive namespaced like /plugin-name:skill-name and update with the plugin.
hardChoices: Publish each skill to a marketplace directly — marketplaces list skills
Add all five skills to every repo's CLAUDE.md so they version with the code
Ship them as an MCP server, the standard unit for sharing skills

questions.prompt: Your org publishes Claude Code plugins in a GitHub repo. How do teammates get them?
choices: Add the marketplace with /plugin marketplace add org/repo, then install individual plugins from it
Adding a marketplace automatically installs every plugin it lists
Clone the repo into node_modules
They can't — only Anthropic's own marketplace exists
questions.reteach: A marketplace is a catalog: add it first, then install each plugin you actually want from it.
hardChoices: Run /plugin install org/repo — installing a repo pulls in its whole catalog
Add the marketplace; each listed plugin then loads on demand automatically
Ask Anthropic to list the repo in the official marketplace first

questions.prompt: You find a tempting plugin in a stranger's marketplace. What do the docs caution?
choices: All plugins run fully sandboxed, so installing is always safe
Plugins can execute code with your user privileges — only install from sources you trust
Anthropic verifies that every third-party plugin works as intended
Only marketplaces can be malicious, never the plugins themselves
questions.reteach: Treat a plugin like installed software — it runs with your privileges, so trust the source before installing.
hardChoices: Plugins are safe once the marketplace itself comes from a trusted source
Only a plugin's MCP servers pose risk; its skills are just markdown
Review the plugin's description — malicious code can't hide elsewhere

questions.prompt: A multi-step procedure you use occasionally, across many different chats. Best home for it?
choices: Custom instructions, so it applies to every conversation
Project knowledge, always loaded in that project
A skill — task-specific, loading only when the task shows up
Re-typing it each time you need it
questions.reteach: Custom instructions apply broadly and project knowledge is always-loaded; skills load only when the task is relevant.
hardChoices: Project knowledge, since procedures belong with standing context
CLAUDE.md, the standard home for multi-step procedures
A plugin — multi-step procedures are too big for a single skill

questions.prompt: Which situation most clearly warrants building a skill?
choices: A checklist you keep pasting into chat again and again
A question you asked exactly once
A one-line fact that fits fine in CLAUDE.md
A tone preference meant for every conversation
questions.reteach: Recurring procedures earn a skill; one-off requests, single facts, and global preferences belong elsewhere.
hardChoices: A tone preference you want applied in every single conversation
A standing fact about your codebase used in every session
Background context a single project should always have loaded
